questions.question: The gaseous envelope surrounding planet Earth is scientifically known as the: (FBISE 2025 Model)
questions.explanation: The atmosphere is the complete gaseous envelope held around Earth by gravity, divided into four primary thermal layers: troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, and thermosphere.

questions.question: Which atmospheric layer lies closest to the Earth's surface (extending from 0 to approximately 12 km) and contains 75% of atmospheric mass? (FBISE 2024-II)
questions.explanation: The troposphere is the lowest atmospheric layer extending up to ~12 km above sea level. Almost all weather phenomena (clouds, rainfall, winds) occur here, and temperature decreases with altitude.

questions.question: In the troposphere, the temperature decreases steadily with increasing altitude at an average lapse rate of: (FBISE 2023-I)
questions.explanation: In the troposphere, the temperature drops with height at an average rate of approximately $-6.5^\circ\text{C}$ per kilometer, decreasing from ~17°C at ground level to about $-55^\circ\text{C}$ at the tropopause.

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary air pollutant? (FBISE 2025 Model)
questions.explanation: $NO_2$ is a major toxic primary pollutant emitted directly from fossil fuel combustion in motor vehicles and thermal power stations, contributing to smog and acid rain.

questions.question: Identify the secondary air pollutant from the following list: (FBISE 2022-II, 2024-I)
questions.explanation: Secondary pollutants are not emitted directly into the air but form via chemical reactions among primary pollutants. Sulphuric acid ($H_2SO_4$) is formed when primary $SO_2$ is oxidized in atmospheric moisture.

questions.question: Which gaseous pollutant binds strongly and irreversibly with blood hemoglobin to form carboxyhemoglobin, blocking oxygen transport? (FBISE 2021-I, 2023-II)
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide ($CO$) has an affinity for hemoglobin over 200 times higher than oxygen. It forms stable carboxyhemoglobin, causing oxygen starvation, asphyxiation, and death.

questions.question: The ozone layer ($O_3$) that absorbs harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from sunlight is primarily located in the: (FBISE 2020-II)
questions.explanation: Ozone is concentrated in the mid-stratosphere between 25 and 30 km above the Earth's surface, where it absorbs lethal solar UV-B and UV-C rays, shielding life on Earth.

questions.question: What happens to the temperature in the stratosphere with increasing altitude? (FBISE 2019-II, Official Test Series)
questions.explanation: In the stratosphere (12 to 50 km), ozone continuously absorbs solar ultraviolet radiation and releases thermal energy, causing the temperature to rise from $-55^\circ\text{C}$ at the base to ~0°C at the stratopause.

questions.question: Rainwater is classified as 'acid rain' when its measured pH falls below: (FBISE 2018-I, 2022-I)
questions.explanation: Unpolluted rainwater naturally has a pH of approximately 5.6 due to dissolved atmospheric $CO_2$ forming weak carbonic acid. Any precipitation with a pH below 5.6 is defined as acid rain.

questions.question: Which two acidic gases are primarily responsible for the formation of acid rain? (FBISE 2017-I, 2021-II)
questions.explanation: Sulphur dioxide ($SO_2$, from burning fossil fuels like coal) and nitrogen oxides ($NO$ and $NO_2$, from vehicle engines) dissolve in cloud water droplets to form strong sulphuric ($H_2SO_4$) and nitric ($HNO_3$) acids.

questions.question: Acid rain attacks and erodes historical buildings, monuments, and statues constructed of marble and limestone ($CaCO_3$) by forming: (FBISE 2016-II)
questions.explanation: $CaCO_3 + H_2SO_4 \to CaSO_4 + H_2O + CO_2\uparrow$. The insoluble marble turns into slightly soluble calcium sulphate (gypsum), which leaches away, causing crumbling known as 'stone leprosy'.

questions.question: Why does acid rain cause massive mortality among freshwater fish in acidified lakes? (FBISE 2015-II, 2020-I)

options.A: It removes all nitrogen gas from water
options.B: It leaches toxic aluminum ($Al^{3+}$) ions from soil, clogging fish gills
options.C: It freezes the surface of lakes solid
options.D: It increases the salt concentration to ocean levels

questions.explanation: Acid rain leaches heavy metals, particularly aluminum ($Al^{3+}$), from surrounding soils into waterways. In fish, aluminum precipitates as aluminum hydroxide over gill membranes, causing asphyxiation and death.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is the chief catalyst responsible for the destruction of stratospheric ozone? (FBISE 2014-I, 2019-I)
questions.explanation: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs, Freons) drift up to the stratosphere where UV radiation breaks carbon-chlorine bonds to release reactive chlorine free radicals ($Cl^\bullet$). Each chlorine radical can catalytically destroy over 100,000 ozone molecules.

questions.question: The prominent greenhouse gases responsible for trapping infrared thermal radiation and causing global warming are: (FBISE 2018-II)
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide ($CO_2$), methane ($CH_4$), water vapor ($H_2O$), nitrous oxide ($N_2O$), and CFCs absorb outgoing longwave infrared radiation re-emitted by Earth's surface, trapping thermal energy.

questions.question: A triatomic allotropic molecule of oxygen produced when electrical discharges or UV light pass through atmospheric oxygen is: (FBISE 2019-I)
questions.explanation: Ozone ($O_3$) is a pale blue, pungent gas formed photochemically or by lightning discharges: $O_2 + O \rightleftharpoons O_3$.

questions.question: What is the coldest thermal region of the Earth's atmosphere, reaching temperatures down to $-93^\circ\text{C}$? (FBISE 2017-II)
questions.explanation: The mesosphere extends from 50 km to 85 km. Because it contains virtually no greenhouse gases or ozone to absorb radiation, temperature drops with altitude, reaching $-93^\circ\text{C}$ at the mesopause.

questions.question: Which of the following human health hazards is directly linked to increased ultraviolet radiation reaching the Earth due to stratospheric ozone depletion?
questions.explanation: Excessive exposure to high-energy solar UV-B rays damages DNA in epidermal skin cells, causing skin cancers (melanomas), and photochemically damages lens proteins in eyes, inducing cataracts.

questions.question: Incineration of municipal domestic solid waste without adequate pollution control releases large amounts of: (FBISE 2016-I)

options.A: Toxic dioxins, furans, and particulate smoke

questions.explanation: Burning chlorinated plastics and municipal waste produces extremely toxic polychlorinated dibenzodioxins and furans, along with heavy smoke and particulate matter.

questions.question: What percentage of clean dry atmospheric air by volume is composed of inert nitrogen ($N_2$) gas?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen ($N_2$) is the most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere, accounting for approximately 78.08% of clean dry air by volume.

questions.question: What percentage of clean dry atmospheric air by volume is composed of oxygen ($O_2$) gas?
questions.explanation: Oxygen ($O_2$) comprises approximately 20.95% (~21%) of Earth's atmosphere by volume, supporting respiration and combustion.

questions.question: What is the concentration of carbon dioxide ($CO_2$) in normal clean ambient air?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide makes up approximately 0.04% (400–420 parts per million) of the ambient atmosphere by volume.

questions.question: The 'ozone hole' is a seasonal severe thinning of the ozone layer observed primarily over which geographic region?
questions.explanation: Extremely cold polar stratospheric clouds (PSCs) over Antarctica create optimal heterogeneous surfaces that accelerate chlorine radical reactions, causing dramatic seasonal ozone depletion each austral spring.

questions.question: Which of the following reactions accurately illustrates the formation of acid rain from sulphur trioxide?
questions.explanation: Sulphur trioxide ($SO_3$) readily dissolves in atmospheric water droplets to form strong sulphuric acid: $SO_3(g) + H_2O(l) \to H_2SO_4(aq)$.

questions.question: Which chemical pollutant is responsible for yellowing of paper and damage to historical paintings and leather?
questions.explanation: $SO_2$ reacts with atmospheric moisture to form sulphurous and sulphuric acids that hydrolyze and weaken cellulose fibers in paper and protein bonds in leather.

questions.question: Photochemical smog is formed on warm, sunny days by the interaction of solar UV rays with which combination of pollutants?

options.A: Nitrogen oxides ($NO_x$) and unburnt volatile organic hydrocarbons

questions.explanation: Photochemical smog is a mixture of secondary oxidants (ozone, PAN, aldehydes) produced when solar UV light photolyzes $NO_2$ in the presence of reactive hydrocarbons.

questions.question: Why is carbon monoxide ($CO$) termed a 'silent killer'?

options.A: It is completely colorless, odorless, non-irritating, and rapidly fatal
options.B: It has an intensely loud hissing sound

questions.explanation: Because $CO$ has no odor, color, or taste, victims cannot detect its presence while inhaling it, causing loss of consciousness without warning.

questions.question: What is the direct consequence of excessive greenhouse gases in the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Accumulation of greenhouse gases traps more thermal infrared radiation in the lower atmosphere, driving rising global mean temperatures, polar ice melting, and sea-level rise.

questions.question: Which of the following oxides of nitrogen is a reddish-brown, pungent gas?
questions.explanation: $NO_2$ is a reddish-brown gas with a sharp, biting odor that is a major constituent of brown photochemical smog hanging over urban areas.

questions.question: How does acid rain damage terrestrial plant foliage and trees?

options.A: It strips protective cuticle wax from leaves and leaches nutrients like calcium and magnesium
options.C: It causes trees to produce excess fruit
options.D: It causes immediate boiling of sap

questions.explanation: Acid precipitation dissolves the protective waxy layer on leaf surfaces, allowing water and pathogens to penetrate while leaching essential mineral nutrients from soil.

questions.question: The global international treaty designed to protect the ozone layer by phasing out the production of CFCs is the:
questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer was adopted in 1987 to phase out production and consumption of chlorofluorocarbons and halons globally.

questions.question: Which catalytic step demonstrates the catalytic destruction of ozone by chlorine radicals ($Cl^\bullet$)?
questions.explanation: The chlorine free radical attacks ozone to generate chlorine monoxide radical and oxygen: $Cl^\bullet + O_3 \to ClO^\bullet + O_2$. Subsequent reaction with free oxygen atoms regenerates $Cl^\bullet$.

questions.question: Which gas is released in substantial quantities from flooded rice paddy fields and ruminant livestock digestion (enteric fermentation)?
questions.explanation: Anaerobic methanogenic bacteria in waterlogged paddy fields and ruminant animal digestive tracts decompose organic matter to produce large quantities of methane ($CH_4$), a potent greenhouse gas.

questions.question: The atmospheric layer extending from 85 km up to approximately 500 km where temperature increases dramatically due to solar X-rays is the:
questions.explanation: In the thermosphere (above 85 km), intense solar X-ray and extreme UV radiation ionizes gas molecules, increasing temperature with altitude up to several hundred degrees Celsius.

questions.question: Which gas is used as an inert shielding gas in welding and filling incandescent electric bulbs?
questions.explanation: Argon ($Ar$) is an unreactive noble gas (0.93% of atmosphere) used as an inert gas shield in arc welding and in light bulbs to prevent tungsten filament oxidation.

questions.question: What is the primary natural source of carbon dioxide in the Earth's atmosphere?

options.A: Aerobic respiration of living organisms and decay of organic matter

questions.explanation: Biological cellular respiration by plants, animals, and microorganisms releases carbon dioxide as glucose is oxidized to produce cellular energy ($ATP$).

questions.question: What happens when catalytic converters are installed in modern automobile exhaust systems?

options.A: Toxic $CO$ and unburnt hydrocarbons are oxidized to harmless $CO_2$ and $H_2O$, and $NO_x$ is reduced to $N_2$
options.C: They eliminate all fuel consumption completely

questions.explanation: Three-way catalytic converters use platinum, palladium, and rhodium catalysts to convert harmful emissions ($CO$, hydrocarbons, and $NO_x$) into harmless nitrogen ($N_2$), carbon dioxide ($CO_2$), and water vapor.

questions.question: Which layer of the atmosphere contains the ionosphere which reflects radio waves back to Earth for telecommunications?
questions.explanation: The ionosphere overlaps the thermosphere and contains high concentrations of free ions and electrons that reflect high-frequency radio waves back to Earth.

questions.question: Which particulate air pollutant released from burning low-grade coal causes black lung disease (anthracosis) in coal miners?
questions.explanation: Inhalation of fine coal dust particles over prolonged periods causes anthracosis (black lung disease), characterized by chronic inflammation and fibrosis of pulmonary lung tissue.

questions.question: What is the effect of global warming on the world's sea levels?

options.A: Sea levels rise due to thermal expansion of ocean water and melting of continental glaciers and ice sheets
options.B: Sea levels drop drastically as water evaporates into outer space

questions.explanation: Warming atmospheric temperatures cause thermal expansion of ocean water and accelerate the melting of land-based polar ice caps and glaciers, causing sea levels to rise.

questions.question: Which indicator gas is commonly monitored to assess air pollution from diesel exhaust and heavy urban traffic?
questions.explanation: Diesel engines emit significant quantities of nitrogen oxides ($NO_x$) and fine particulate soot ($PM_{2.5}$), making them prime indicators of urban vehicular air pollution.
